CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DATE OF BIRTH: [redacted date]
MEDICAL RECORD: [redacted ID]
SPECIMEN TYPE: Fetal skin tissue
DATE COLLECTED: [redacted date]
DATE RECEIVED: [redacted date]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal chromosomal abnormality testing - confirmation of prior prenatal diagnosis

TEST PERFORMED
Karyotype analysis

METHODOLOGY
Fetal skin fibroblasts were cultured and harvested according to standard protocols. G-banded chromosome analysis was performed at 450-550 band resolution. Twenty metaphases were analyzed.

RESULT
47,XX,+21

INTERPRETATION
This karyotype demonstrates trisomy 21 in all cells analyzed, confirming the prior prenatal diagnosis of Down syndrome. The presence of three copies of chromosome 21 is consistent with the clinical diagnosis.

RECURRENCE RISK
The empiric recurrence risk for trisomy 21 in future pregnancies depends on maternal age at delivery:
- Maternal age <30: approximately 1%
- Maternal age 35: approximately 1.5%
- Maternal age 40: approximately 5%
- Maternal age 45: approximately 15%

Parental karyotype analysis may be considered to exclude a balanced translocation, although this is found in only 3-4% of trisomy 21 cases.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss recurrence risks and reproductive options
2. Prenatal diagnosis (chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis) is available for subsequent pregnancies
3. Preimplantation genetic testing may be considered as an alternative reproductive option

This analysis was performed in a CLIA-certified laboratory.

Reported by: [redacted name], Ph.D., FACMG
Laboratory Director
